ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS
November 202 4
DOB ISSUES MONTHLY ENFORCEMENT BULLETIN
Report Highlights DOB Enforcement Outcomes from November 2024 to Deter
Bad Actors and Keep New Yorkers Safe
New York, NY – The New York City Department of Buildings released its enforcement
bulletin for November 2024, which provides highlights of the agency’s actions to
sanction and deter bad actors in the construction industry through the enforcement of
safety laws and codes of conduct. Today’s bulletin includes summaries of DOB-
imposed disciplinary actions, including penalties, license suspensions and revocations.
The actions below represent a portion of DOB’s overall work to enforce the City’s
building codes and safety laws, in addition to the thousands of inspections conducted
and violations issued by the agency each month for illegal building and construction
conditions.
DOB completed several major enforcement actions in November, including:
 8 violations and $110,000 in penalties issued for Failure to Safeguard
construction sites at 8 locations.
 19 violations and $407,625 in penalties, including daily penalties, issued for
illegal building alterations at 3 locations.
 1 violation and $10,000 in penalties issued to 1 individual for failure to carry out
the duties of a construction superintendent.
Below are individual enforcement highlights for November 2024:
Construction and Design Professionals
 DOB’s Special Enforcement Team (SET) audited multiple professionally certified
applications submitted by Registered Architect Oscar Fuertes and found major
code non-compliances, including filing Alteration Type 2 applications despite
proposing changes in use, egress, and/or occupancy, which require Alteration
Type 1 applications for a new or amended Certificate of Occupancy; proposing
plans that fail to show two exits from the cellar; failure to show any notes and
shoring details for proposed structural work; failure to provide a flood hazard map
and supporting data; and various other violations of code and rules, including the
Zoning Resolution, Building Code, and Administrative Code. Based on the audits,

SET offered a voluntary surrender of Professional Certification and Directive 14
privileges which the Respondent agreed to.
 General Contractor Angeline Pena-Levi was disciplined for having been issued a
large number of sustained summonses at sites for which she was responsible.
The respondent agreed to a two-year suspension, correction of uncorrected
summonses, and 18 months of probation.
 Master Fire Suppression Contractor Jeffrey S. Handler was issued a warning
letter reminding him that he must retain 51 percent ownership of his master fire
suppression business.
Bronx
 $181,875 in penalties issued to Mohammed Shakeer Khan for violations
recorded at 1419 Bryant Avenue. DOB inspectors issued violations for illegal
alterations after finding the second floor, a legal 1-family dwelling, was converted
to a 5-family with the addition of 4 illegal Single Room Occupancies (SROs).
Additionally, inspectors issued violations for storage of combustible materials in
the boiler room and for exposed electrical wires in the second-floor hallway.
 $36,500 in penalties issued to Bradley E. Simmons for violations recorded at
1256 Teller Avenue. DOB inspectors issued violations for illegal alterations after
finding the legal 2-family dwelling converted to an illegal 7-family by the addition
of 5 Single Room Occupancies (SROs). DOB inspectors also issued violations
for work without a permit for full-height partitions constructed on the 2nd floor,
water and waste lines on the 1st floor, and garage work that included the addition
of 2 bathrooms, installation of gas lines, and electrical wiring work.
 $25,000 in penalties issued to 214-217 LLC for violations recorded at 714 East
217 Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to maintain emergency
egress of the neighboring property when inspectors observed the fire escape
egress route leading directly through an active construction site.
 $18,750 in penalties issued to Goodman Realty Group, Corp. for violations
recorded at 896 E 167th Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for the condition
of a retaining wall on the premises that was observed leaning into an adjacent
property.
 $11,250 in penalties issued to New Line Construction LLC for violations recorded
at 2414 Cambreleng Avenue. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to
safeguard after observing workers on a suspended scaffold without fall
protection, and for failure to notify the Department of the scaffold installation.

 $10,000 in penalties issued to Omnibuild Construction Inc. for violations recorded
at 586 Gerard Avenue. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard
after a portion of the adjacent property collapsed into the construction site during
excavation operations.
 $10,000 in penalties issued to New Line Construction LLC for violations recorded
at 2621 Grand Avenue. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard
after a worker fell off a scaffold, and for not providing a DOB inspector with
requested documents showing that the worker was provided with proper training
to use the scaffold equipment.
 $10,000 in penalties issued to Concrete Contracting Con for violations recorded
at 1824 Anthony Ave. DOB inspectors issued violations to the contractor for
inadequate Construction Superintendent log keeping.
 $10,000 in penalties issued to Robert Casalapro for violations recorded at 1851
Phelan Place. DOB inspectors issued violations for the submission of false
documents in the filing of a Certificate of Correction for a previously-issued
summons.
Brooklyn
 $129,250 in penalties issued to Qiu Lan Lin for violations recorded at 745 45th
Street. DOB inspectors issued violations after finding the legal 2-family dwelling
illegally converted to a 10-family with the addition of 8 Single Room Occupancies
(SROs) that were being occupied for transient use.
 $60,000 in penalties imposed on 1962 CIA LLC for violations recorded at 8161
New Utrecht Avenue. DOB inspectors issued sign violations for failure to obtain
permits or engage a licensed sign hanger, and for failure to bear the UL
classification mark or date of sign erection.

 $10,000 in penalties issued to RIG Kingland Services Inc. for violations recorded
at 19 Rockwell Place. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard
during demolition operations after bricks fell onto an adjacent construction site.
 $5,000 in penalties issued to 1375 E 18 LLC, for violations recorded at 1371 E
18th Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for transient use in one apartment
of the multiple dwelling building, and lack of automatic sprinklers and a Class J
fire alarm system.
 $2,800 in penalties imposed on 1339 Fulton Street Realty, LLC, for violations
recorded at 1339 Fulton Street. DOB inspectors issued violations to the owner for
installing illuminated flashing signs prohibited by the Zoning Resolution, and for
exceeding the legal size and projection limits for a business sign.
 A petition to padlock the property at 120 and 122 Sapphire Street was filed by
DOB at OATH after inspectors observed commercial vehicle storage and use of
a contractor’s yard in the yard of a 1-family house located within a residential
district.

Manhattan
 $70,000 in penalties imposed on Gammon Enterprises LLC for violations
recorded at 461 Park Avenue South. DOB inspectors issued violations to the
respondent for illegally displaying an outdoor sign without a permit, failure to
engage a licensed sign hanger, failure to register as an Outdoor Advertising
Agency, and for exceeding the sign surface area and height limitations for a sign
in the zoning district.

 $35,000 in penalties issued to Majestic Property Management Corp. for violations
recorded at 251 West 98th Street. DOB Inspectors issued violations to the
building owner for failure to institute required pedestrian safety measures after
filing an unsafe façade report with the Department.
 $25,000 in penalties issued to Gilbane Building Company for violations recorded
at 1901 1st Avenue. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard the
job site after approximately 100 feet of construction fence collapsed and injured
four pedestrians, and inspectors found that yodock barriers were not filled as per
the manufacturer’s specifications.
 $22,250 in penalties issued to Vinbaytel Developments LLC for violations
recorded at 16 West 18th Street. DOB inspectors issued multiple safety violations
at the new building construction project work site after finding there was no Site
Safety Manager nor Coordinator present, and no safety monitoring program.
Inspectors also observed a supported scaffold at the site that was missing stairs,
unsecured fire extinguishers with missing and/or expired tags, and lack of
required viewing panels on the construction fence.
 $12,500 in penalties issued to Artimus Construction Inc. for violations recorded at
88 East 127th Street. Inspectors issued violations following an incident where a
worker on the ground floor was hit by falling formwork from the roof, and
inspectors determined that no overhead protection was provided, contrary to the
project’s site safety plan.
 $10,000 in penalties issued to Roundsquare Builders LLC for violations recorded
at 107 Bank Street. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to have a
Construction Superintendent on the job site.
 $6,250 in penalties issued to 413-415 West 52nd Street. DOB inspectors issued
violations after a decorative stone at the 4th story level fell onto the public
sidewalk, and inspectors observed the decorative stones around the 3rd story
window were also in disrepair.
 DOB inspectors issued a closure order at 560 West 170th Street, apartment 1A,
after finding a commercial clothing store operation being operating from the
apartment. A recent reinspection of the apartment determined that the
commercial activity had ceased in compliance with DOB orders. As a result, DOB
is rescinding the closure order.
Queens
 $60,625 in penalties issued to Wei Ai Hua for violations recorded at 138-22 Elder
Avenue. DOB inspectors issued violations for illegal alterations after altering the

3-family dwelling to a 7-family by adding 4 Single Room Occupancies (SROs)
with locking devices on the doors, and violations for work without a permit for
erecting full height partitions to subdivide the room.
 $10,000 in penalties issued to Best NY Contracting Inc. for violations recorded at
147-14 84th Road. DOB inspections issued violations for failure to properly
safeguard the adjacent property while active façade work was underway.
 A petition to padlock the property at 132-03 Ruby Street was filed at OATH after
inspectors observed dead vehicle storage, commercial vehicle storage, and use
of a contractor’s yard at the location, which is located in a residential district.
 The owners of 75-20 Blake Avenue signed a stipulation agreement with DOB
agreeing to cease the illegal use of their property as a contractor’s yard and for
storage of building materials.

 Following DOB’s findings of a commercial auto repair business, dead storage of
motor vehicles, and junk salvage storage at 173-10 108th Avenue, a closure
order was executed in 2013 for the property, which is located in a residential
district. A recent reinspection determined that that the lot has been recently
cleared of the commercial activity, and a recission of the closure order is being
prepared.
Staten Island
 $10,000 in penalties issued to Kaci NY Corp. for violations recorded at 5 Dalmere
Road. DOB inspectors issued violations for failure to safeguard after a brick wall
collapsed at the permitted job site.
